newsitem.title: USA: Closing arguments over in Reynolds trial.
newsitem.headline: Closing arguments over in Reynolds trial.

text.p: Plaintiffs attorneys on Friday afternoon ended more than five hours of closing arguments on Friday afternoon in a wrongful death lawsuit filed by the family of a deceased smoker against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.

Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman immediately began instructing the six-member jury in matter of law after which they were expected to begin deliberations in the widely watched case. Dana Raulerson, the sister of smoker Jean Connor, filed the lawsuit on behalf of Connor's estate and her children. Connor died in 1995 of lung cancer.
Plaintiffs Attorney Norwood "Woody" Wilner told jurors Reynolds had taken the unusual position of selling dangerous products and then suggesting people should not have bought them.

Reynolds "sells candy with razor blades inside to anyone who wants to buy...then suggests that they shouldn't have bought that candy," Wilner said in response to Reynolds claim that Jean Connor had chosen to smoke. Wilner was making a short rebuttal to closing arguments from Reynolds' attorney Paul Crist, who said Connor knew about the potential health risks of smoking but chose to do it anyway.
Wilner attacked Crist's contention that Reynolds had no duty to warning the public because the potential health risks were widely known in the United States.
"It's like saying there's no need to label a poison, because everyone knows poison is dangerous," he said.

Referring to internal company documents introduced at the trial in which Reynolds researchers suggested publishing company research, Wilner said they were evidence that Reynolds own scientists had tried to tell top company officials to publish their findings on the smoking-cancer link.
"It's a scientist who knows there's been a coverup and is trying to tell the head guys we should say something before we get caught with our hands in the cookie jar," he said.
